LESSON: MANAGING RESOURCES:

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: General
Strand: Sadachaar (Social Ethics)
Topic 5.1: Managing Resources:
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Managing Resources:, part of Sadachaar (Social Ethics) in Grade 6 General.

Key inquiry question: How can we take care of resources in school and community? 2. Why is it important for an individual to take care of resources?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. name different types of resources,

2. research and classify different types of commonly used resources,

3. compare and adopt various strategies from other countries to manage resources,

4. discuss with peers appropriate use of resources,

5. plan for and share resources with the less fortunate in society,

6. download and use time management applications from digital devices,

7. initiate campaign with peers to motivate peers to be punctual in all school activities,

8. create a hypothetical budget with priority items to be purchased within the available funds,

9. design posters indicating switching off the electric appliances/turning off the taps after use at school/home/community centres, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. name different types of resources,
2. research and classify different types of commonly used resources,
3. compare and adopt various strategies from other countries to manage resources,
4. discuss with peers appropriate use of resources,
5. plan for and share resources with the less fortunate in society,
6. download and use time management applications from digital devices,
7. initiate campaign with peers to motivate peers to be punctual in all school activities,
8. create a hypothetical budget with priority items to be purchased within the available funds,
9. design posters indicating switching off the electric appliances/turning off the taps after use at school/home/community centres, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Managing Resources: together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: Learner develops a sense of initiative and entrepreneurship skill when creating a hypothetical budget with

priority items to be purchased with the available funds.

• Creativity: Learner enhances decision making skills when modelling the managing of resources prudently for sustainable

development.

Values:
• Responsibility: Learner practices self-drive when initiating a campaign with peers to motivate peers to be punctual in all

school activities.

• Love: Learner extends love by sharing when visiting a Home for the less fortunate to appreciate the value of responsible use

of food.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Community service learning: Learner engages in community service when visiting a Home for the less fortunate to

appreciate the value of responsible use of food.

• Education for Sustainable Development (ESD): Learner enhances financial literacy when creating a hypothetical budget with

priority items to be purchased with the available funds.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Learner can relate the skills of designing posters indicating switching off the electric appliances/turning off the taps after use at

school/home/community centres to the skills of designing posters learnt in Creative Arts.
